When someone’s sharing with me during counseling, I realize halfway through I’ve drifted, not because I don’t care—Lord knows I do—but because a sound, a thought, something just pulls my attention away. Preparing sermons feels overwhelming; I avoid it until the last minute because organizing my thoughts takes so much mental effort. I’ve lost my Bible, notes, even my keys multiple times this month.  

I do feel anxious sometimes—worried about responsibilities, my family, the congregation—but that’s not what’s making me space out or lose things. The distraction comes from outside: a noise, a sudden idea, something new that catches my curiosity. It’s not that I’m ruminating. In fact, when I *am* worried, I can sometimes focus better, ironically. The problem is holding steady on anything that’s routine, even if I’m not stressed about it. It’s been this way since I was a kid—just part of how my mind works.

It’s not that I don’t care—far from it—but my mind is racing with worries. What if I preach the wrong message? What if I let someone down? I used to think I was just disorganized, but now I see it’s tied to this constant tension. It’s not distraction from new or exciting things—it’s my own thoughts getting in the way. The more I worry, the harder it is to focus. It feels like my mind’s always full, but I can’t calm it down.

I’ve missed a couple of deadlines, not because I didn’t care, but because I lost track of time or forgot to follow up on emails. Same with personal stuff—bills, phone calls, even meeting friends. There’s also this constant low-level buzz, like my brain won’t shut off. I don’t feel anxious, exactly—more like I can’t sit still mentally, even when I’m not worried about anything in particular. It’s like my attention just *drifts*, pulled toward anything new or stimulating.

I’ve been feeling really overwhelmed lately, like I can’t keep up no matter how hard I try. At school, I’ll start giving instructions to my students and realize halfway through that I’ve lost my train of thought or didn’t finish what I meant to say. It’s frustrating because I plan my lessons, but when the day gets busy, things slip—papers don’t get graded on time, or I forget to assign homework I meant to. I don’t know if it’s the workload or just me, but even at home, simple things like meal planning or paying bills feel like they need more focus than I can muster.

I’ve always been someone who moves quickly—my husband jokes that I never stop, like I’m wired to keep going. I pace when I’m thinking, or fidget during staff meetings. It’s not that I don’t care; I care a lot, especially about my kids and doing well at work. But trying to focus on tasks that take a long time, like writing reports or grading essays, makes me want to escape. I’ll switch to something easier just to feel like I’ve accomplished *something.*  

I do worry from time to time—about deadlines, whether I missed an email, if the kids are okay—but I can’t say it’s constant. Most days I just feel scattered, like my mind’s in too many places at once. I can’t pinpoint exactly when it started, but it’s been like this for a while.

I just can’t seem to stay on track. Organizing my day, my classroom, even my thoughts feels overwhelming. Paperwork from school? I put it off because focusing for long stretches is exhausting.

I’m always moving—fidgeting, pacing during prep time, or cleaning obsessively at home. My husband says I never sit still, but it’s not because I’m worried. If anything, I feel most restless when I *should* be concentrating, especially on routine or boring tasks. The anxiety I do have—like over job performance—is newer and stems *from* these ongoing failures, not the other way around. I get distracted not because I’m ruminating, but because something new catches my eye—a noise, an idea—and suddenly I’m off track.
